character_sheet: A tameable, skittish grazer: a 6x6x13 body with a chest wedge, a long raked neck with a throat fluff, a cube head with a nose, a mouth, two ears and two three-segment antlers, four legs of four or five pieces down to a hoof, and a stub tail (ModelGazelle.java:101-269, 34 parts). 15 HP, speed 0.3 and no attack (Gazelle.java:82-87). It flees monsters within 8 blocks and players within 12 (:73, :76), panics when hurt (:75), is tempted by wheat (:74) and tamed by it one time in two (:226-249); tamed it follows its owner (:72), sits on a right-click (:277-282), is untamed with glass (:251-265) and takes at most 10 per hit (:210-216). It grazes: hurt or on a 1-in-750 tick it scans up to ten blocks for carrots, potatoes or grass, walks there, eats the block with a burp and heals (:89-94, :150-182); every 250 ticks or so it drifts toward another gazelle (:184-189). It spawns between y 50 and 100 on dirt or grass (:288-294; ModEntities.java:385-386), breeds on a crystal apple (:325-327) and its fawn inherits the owner (:340-348). Read it as a deer: a light diagonal trot, the ears flicking, the tail wagging, the head down to graze.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig, x0.5 as a baby (GazelleRenderer.java:28, :40-41; shadow 0.45, :30) on a 64x64 sheet (ModelGazelle.java:271), gazelletexture.png (GazelleRenderer.java:22); the hitbox is 0.6 x 1.8 (ModEntities.java:385-386). The original's ModelGazelle(0.65f) argument was the wingspeed (ModelGazelle.java:24), not a scale.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.12 = 0.377 rad (22 deg) x the walking speed above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1, added to each piece's rest (front: 0.297 / -0.074 / -0.409 / 0; rear: 0 / 0.185 / -0.074 / -0.409 / 0); 0 below the threshold
groups.plain: the four legs swing fore and aft as stiff chains, every piece of a leg together: the left front with the right rear one way, the right front with the left rear the other — a diagonal trot
groups.math: a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 1.1 * 0.65) * pi * 0.12 * amount : 0; lfleg1..4.xRot = rest + a; rfleg1..4.xRot = rest - a; lrleg1..5.xRot = rest - a; rrleg1..5.xRot = rest + a
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 gates it
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.1 x 0.65 = 0.715: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.715 = 8.79 ticks

groups.name: ears
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (4 deg) about 1.57 rad plus the head's yaw, both ears together
groups.plain: the ears flick gently in step, riding the head's turn
groups.math: e = cos(t * 0.5) * pi * 0.02; lear.yRot = rear.yRot = 1.57 + head.yRot + e
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.5 (no wingspeed term): the natural period is 12.6 ticks

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.06 = 0.188 rad (11 deg) about a 1.0 rad rest; skipped (the last value held) while the entity is in the crouching pose
groups.plain: the tail wags slowly up and down at all times
groups.phase: the branch on isCrouching() (the CROUCHING pose, one a mob is never given) holds the last angle
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.1: the natural period is 62.8 ticks

behaviour: One gait rhythm above a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (ModelGazelle.java:276-297): the eighteen leg pieces swing 22 degrees x the walking speed about their rests at 0.715 rad/tick (an 8.8-tick period), each leg a stiff chain, the left front with the right rear and the right front with the left rear — a diagonal trot at the 0.3 walk (Gazelle.java:53).

Two unscaled rhythms: the ears flick 4 degrees at 0.5 rad/tick over the head's yaw (:299, :302-303) and the tail wags 11 degrees about 1.0 rad at 0.1 rad/tick, a 63-tick period (:311-313) — the one state branch, which skips the wag while the entity is in the crouching pose (a pose a mob never takes), so in practice it always runs.

The head, nose and mouth yaw together with the look at 0.45 of the head yaw and never pitch (:300-301); the six antler segments follow the head's yaw (:304-309). The chest, body, neck and throat fluff are static.
The sit toggle (Gazelle.java:277-282, setInSittingPose) and the graze (:150-182: the walk to the block, the bite, the burp) draw no pose today — the model has no sitting branch and no head pitch.
